u to the computer, own settings UI, queue and stop.
# dsh-phononspeak
> **Language:** English · Česky
A local, Czech-first voice channel for a DeepSeek Harness agent. The agent can read a short summary
of its answer aloud, and it can call you back to the computer when it needs a decision — with a spok

en
sentence, a macOS notification and a banner with "Jsem tady". Speech is synthesised on your machi

ne by
one of four engines, queued with priorities, stoppable, and configured from its own Settings p

age
inside Harness. No cloud TTS, no API key, no upload of the text.
## Why

An agent that works for minutes at a time is a bad thing to stare at. This plugin exists for two
mom
ents, and nothing else:
| The job | What happens | What it buys you |
| **Read the answer aloud** | The model calls `dsh_phononspeak action=summary` with a 1–3 sentence C

zech summary; the plugin speaks it | You keep your hands on the work and still hear the result |
| *
*Call you to the computer** | The agent needs approval or an answer → a short spoken line, a macOS n
otification, a banner with "Jsem tady" | You do not have to watch the screen, and you do not miss th
a banner with "Jsem tady" | You do not have to watch the screen, and you do not miss the question |

Everything else is deliberately absent: the plugin does not narrate reasoning, does not read code,
U
RLs or long lists, and stays silent until it has something worth saying.
## Features

- **Summary reading** — one tool call, one short Czech paragraph. Optionally after every answer
(`au

toSummary`), which also switches on the matching instruction in the system prompt.
- **Written to be

spoken** — before synthesis, Markdown and code fences are removed (a removed block is
announced, no

t silently skipped), URLs and file paths become words, emoji go away, numbers, dates,
money and unit

s become Czech numerals with the right gender, dotted Czech abbreviations are expanded,
and English

terms are transliterated. The result is split into sentences of at most 220 characters.
- **Attentio

n calls** — a spoken line, a macOS notification (`osascript`) and an in-UI banner with
"Jsem tady".

Optionally repeated every 15, 30 or 60 seconds until you acknowledge it.
- **A real queue** — attent

ion > question > summary > manual > test. Nothing overlaps; two
announcements in the same second no

longer talk over each other.
- **A real stop** — `action=stop` aborts the running synthesis, kills t

he player process, clears the
queue and the repeat timer. Jobs from before the stop are discarded, n

ot resumed.
[该节后续省略]
### Requirements
| Requirement | Why |
| DeepSeek Harness with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools >=0.1.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` | The peer range this package d

eclares. |
| Node.js >= 22 | `engines.node` in `package.json`. |
| macOS | For `say`, `afplay` and `

osascript`. On Linux and Windows only the in-page player and the non-Apple engines work. |
| Python
3.10 or newer with `venv` | Only for Supertonic and Pocket TTS Czech. Piper and `say` need no Python
. The interpreter is discovered and its version verified before a virtualenv is created, because a `
python3` shim that answers 3.8 builds half a dependency tree and then fails. |
Two packaging details matter when something does not load:
- The peer range is deliberately open. A Harness loader silently skips a plugin whose peer range is

not satisfied — the `^0.1.0-rc.6` ranges of the older `dsh-agent-voice` and `dsh-voice-studio` are
a

n example: they do not match a 0.2.x runtime, so those plugins never start and nothing is logged.
-

The package has no `prepare` or `install` lifecycle script. pnpm runs build scripts for Git
dependen
cies only after an explicit approval, so the package ships prebuilt `lib/*.js`.
## Honest limitations
- **The Pocket model speaks like a parliament.** It was trained on 976 hours of Czech parliamentary
speech: adults, formal register, many men. Conversational Czech, children and casual word order are

weaker. Good narration, not a voice actor.
- **Piper mispronounces Czech words.** Measured on the ra

w engine: "Vltava" comes out as "Voltava" and
"Kč" as "káčej". The normaliser rewrites money before

synthesis, so "Kč" reaches the engine as
"korun"; place names and loanwords are not rewritten, and t

hose still slip. Piper is the cheapest
engine, not the best one.
- **Supertonic has no streaming API

.** We stream by sentence: the first sentence is synthesised and
played while the next one is being

made. That keeps the first sound early, but it is not a
sample-level stream.
- **macOS-first.** Linu

x and Windows have no `say`, no `afplay` and no `osascript`. The engines still
work, but sound comes

from the page, and notification plus repeat-until-acknowledged are macOS
features. When no tab is v

isible on a non-macOS host, the system-playback path has nothing to play.
- **Pocket costs about 1 G

B** of Python and torch before the 438 MB model. Choose Supertonic or Piper
if that is too much.
- *

*The plugin speaks what it is told.** It normalises and shortens text, but it cannot tell whether
th

e model's summary is a good summary. A vague summary is read out as confidently as a precise one.
-

**Speed is engine-dependent.** The host clamps every value to 0.7–1.6; `say` maps it to words per
mi
nute, Piper falls back to its default rate if its CLI rejects the flag, and Pocket TTS Czech has no

speed control at all, so the slider does nothing on that engine.
- **Paragraph-level, not conversati

on-level.** There is no history of what was read, no per-message
"read this" button, no keyboard sho

rtcut and no slash command in 0.1.0.
- **The queue is bounded.** At most 24 waiting jobs: beyond tha

t the oldest waiting job is dropped, and
a single job is capped at 20 000 characters before normalis

oldest waiting job is dropped, and
a single job is capped at 20 000 characters before normalisation.
## Privacy

The text you hear never leaves the machine: synthesis is local and there is no telemetry. The only
m

etadata kept — engine, duration, error — lives in memory and is published to the local page; the
spo

ken text is never written to a log. What is stored, where, and how to delete all of it:
docs/PRIVACY

text is never written to a log. What is stored, where, and how to delete all of it:
docs/PRIVACY.md.
